comment: NIM `decorates` fixture — the pragma-TEMPLATE class at rung R3 (2026-10-23), pinned in BOTH directions. THE POSITIVE HALF: a declaration carrying a pragma that names a FILE-LOCAL `{.pragma.}` template is an APPLIED CALLABLE in a pragma position, and the dictionary's decorator is exactly that (src/ast/types.ts:131-144, direction decorated declaration -> decorator). THE NEGATIVE HALF is the point of the fixture: a BUILTIN DIRECTIVE pragma (`{.inline.}`, `{.cdecl.}`, `{.raises.}`) is passive compiler metadata and must NEVER become a row — without this half, a partial implementation that swept all 33,266 pragma name sites into `decorates` would pass. The census that made this cell IMPLEMENTED rather than RULED is validation/m14/measurements/nim-extended-census.json: it measured the falsifier of the intended ontological ruling (294 applied callables in pragma positions, 0.9 % of the pragma population) and the ruling was WITHDRAWN BY ITS OWN FALSIFIER.

expectSymbols.name: myMarker
expectSymbols.comment: `template myMarker() {.pragma.}` is the template that makes a pragma name a callable

expectSymbols.name: decorated
expectSymbols.comment: the decorated declaration is a published symbol, which is the contract's precondition for any row

expectSymbols.name: directiveOnly
expectSymbols.comment: the negative twin: a declaration whose only pragma is a BUILTIN directive

expectRelationships.comment: THE POSITIVE HALF. Source is the decorated declaration's published spelling, target is the file-local pragma template, and the line is the PRAGMA NAME's own line (the naming node), not the declaration's. `decoratorConstruct` is what tells a consumer this row is the applied-callable class rather than an annotation sweep

forbidRelationships.comment: THE NEGATIVE HALF, ON THE TARGET: `{.inline.}` is a compiler directive — passive metadata, not an applied callable — and it must never become a decorates row. A partial fix that emits every pragma name fails here
THE NEGATIVE HALF, ON THE SOURCE: the declaration whose only pragma is a directive carries NO decorates row at all
the pragma template's OWN declaration carries `{.pragma.}` — the marker that DEFINES a pragma template, not an application to it — so it must not decorate itself

expectDecorators.comment: the pragma NAME stays on the symbol's decorators payload as well: it is the evidence, and the row above says what it MEANS (an applied callable), not that the name is deleted from metadata
a directive pragma is symbol metadata and only that
